title: bootBuildImage push on Windows fails to run 'docker-credential-gcloud' (CreateProcess error=2)
errorSample:
java.io.IOException: Cannot run program "docker-credential-gcloud": CreateProcess error=2, The system cannot find the file specified
	at java.base/java.lang.ProcessBuilder.start(ProcessBuilder.java:1112)
	at java.base/java.lang.ProcessBuilder.start(ProcessBuilder.java:1046)
	at org.gradle.internal.classpath.Instrumented.start(Instrumented.java:315)
	at org.springframework.boot.buildpack.platform.docker.configuration.CredentialHelper.start(CredentialHelper.java:88)
	at org.springframework.boot.buildpack.platform.docker.configuration.CredentialHelper.get(CredentialHelper.java:54)
	at org.springframework.boot.buildpack.platform.docker.configuration.DockerRegistryConfigAuthentication.computeCredentialsFromHelper(DockerRegistryConfigAuthentication.java:129)

appliesTo.versions: 4.0.1 on Windows 11 with Google Cloud SDK credential helper provided as a .cmd file; fix PR milestoned 3.5.11

sources.license: Facts summarized from a public GitHub issue/PR; short error excerpt quoted.
Facts summarized from a public GitHub issue/PR; short error excerpt quoted.

symptom: The image builds, but pushing to Google Artifact Registry with bootBuildImage fails to authenticate: looking up the credential helper throws IOException "Cannot run program "docker-credential-gcloud": CreateProcess error=2, The system cannot find the file specified", and the push is then attempted without credentials. The helper is configured in credHelpers of the Docker config.json.
cause: On Windows the Google Cloud SDK ships the helper as docker-credential-gcloud.cmd. A batch file cannot be started by its bare name through Java ProcessBuilder; it must be run through cmd /c. The plugin has code to prepend cmd /c on Windows, but it calls command(...) twice so the second call overwrites the first and the prefix is lost.
fixSummary: Upgrade to a Spring Boot release that contains the fix (PR milestoned 3.5.11). Workarounds: pass the registry credentials directly in the plugin configuration (docker.publishRegistry with username/password or token), make the helper available as an executable (.exe) on PATH, or push with docker push instead of bootBuildImage.
